subject: Mythology
title: Vodou: African Mythology in Haiti
description: A quick win: understand Vodou: African Mythology in Haiti.

hook.text: Vodou is not Hollywood voodoo dolls. It is a real religion with millions of followers, born from African mythology.

buildup.text: Enslaved Fon and Ewe people from West Africa carried their spirits (lwa) to Haiti and blended them with Catholic saints.

discovery.text: In 1791, a Vodou ceremony at Bois Caiman sparked the Haitian Revolution — the only successful slave revolt in history.

twist.text: Hollywood turned Vodou into horror. Real Vodou is a healing practice with priests, ceremonies, and ancestral honor.

climax.text: Vodou was officially recognized as a religion in Haiti in 2003, ending centuries of persecution and misrepresentation.

punchline.text: The religion Hollywood fears most helped launch history's only slave revolution.

quiz.question: What role did Vodou play in the Haitian Revolution of 1791?
options: It had no involvement in political events
A Vodou ceremony at Bois Caiman sparked the revolution
Vodou priests negotiated peace with the French colonizers
